messages:
incident-bot: ALERT fired: latency.slo.p99 > 1800ms for service=redwood-runtime (region=us-east-1)
incident-bot: alert_id=ALRT-1745009991, severity=page, fired_at=1745009991
incident-bot: snapshot: p95=720ms p99=1850ms qps=5200 error_rate=0.15%
incident-bot: link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/latency?panelId=9&from=now-5m

Anika: ack
Anika: taking lead. Paging PD and kicking off triage. @Jorge can you look at model-worker queues?

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident ALRT-1745009991 triggered. Page sent to Anika. Escalation policy: oncall -> secondary in 4m.

Jorge: joining. I see tail latency ballooning in the model-worker service, but CPU and mem look normal. There is a big async dispatch backlog between frontend and workers.

Suresh: note: we rolled out runtime v3.5.2 to canary ~20m ago, traffic ramped to 25%. Might be related.

Anika: which endpoints are showing the worst p99?

Jorge: quick PromQL:
``
sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{le="1"}[1m])) by (route)
```
Jorge: hotspots: /v1/generate-chat, /v1/embeddings-large, /v1/batch-rerank — combined ~18% of traffic but ~60% of p99 events.

Suresh: propose immediate mitigations:
1) pause canary / rollback to v3.5.1
2) divert heavy embedding traffic to cpu-backed fallback pool
3) temporarily enable degraded fast-path (shorter generations) for free-tier customers
4) reduce batch windows and disable tail-aggregation for chat routes

Anika: agree on 1 & 2 first. Suresh, roll back canary. Jorge, add diversion rule for embeddings.

Suresh: issuing rollback:
```
redwood deploy set-traffic --service redwood-runtime --canary 0 --stable v3.5.1
```
Suresh: rollback job started (job_id=rb-1745010020).

Jorge: adding routing rule to divert embeddings:
```
redwood routing add-rule --match route=/v1/embeddings* --region us-east-1 --target=cpu-embeddings-pool --priority=100
```
Jorge: rule applied, new embeddings requests will route to cpu pool.

pagerduty: Anika acknowledged the page. No escalation occurred at 4m.

Anika: posting status update: "Investigating increased tail latency in us-east-1 impacting chat & embeddings. Mitigations applied: rollback canary, routing adjustments. No data loss. Updates every 15m."

OpsRotation: joining for handoff. @Anika what's the plan if p99 remains >1500ms after rollback and diversion?

Anika: handoff to OpsRotation at 1745010200. Summary:
- suspected root: scheduling regression in async dispatcher introduced by v3.5.2 under bursty load
- actions taken: rolled back canary, diverted embeddings, reduced batch windows on hot routes
- current: p95 ~430ms, p99 ~900-1100ms; overall affected volume ~15-20% in us-east-1; error rate stable
- impacted customers: CustomerX, CustomerY (notified)

OpsRotation: ack. I'll keep PD incident open, run perf traces against v3.5.2 in a staging cluster, and prepare runbook steps for escalation.

ReleaseBot: locking release v3.5.2 in CI to prevent further rollout until RCA.

Suresh: rollback finished at 1745010305. Monitoring telemetry.

Jorge: worker queues drained, backlog cleared, p99 trending downward.

incident-bot: ALRT-1745009991 marked mitigated at 1745010410 (status: mitigated). Observed p99 under 1200ms post-mitigations; continuing watch.

OpsRotation: opening incident doc and assigning postmortem owner to Suresh. Please include perf diffs, traces, and the routing rule change.

Suresh: will own postmortem. I'll gather trace flamegraphs, canary artifacts, and the config diffs.

Anika: thanks all, excellent coordination. :thumbsup:
